newsitem.title: USA: CME board to appoint task force on broker groups.
newsitem.headline: CME board to appoint task force on broker groups.

text.p: Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) directors voted at Wednesday's board meeting to appoint a task force to study broker associations and groups, the exchange said on Friday.
One source on the board said that within the next week the CME's executive committee will present to the board a list of candidates to serve on the task force.
Recommendations from the task force will be made within 90 days, he said.
The floor trading practices of some broker groups or associations, particularly for-profit groups which hire salaried brokers, have been recently criticized by locals and members.

Broker groups and associations consist of two or more floor brokers who register at a futures exchange as one entity in order to share expenses, and in some cases, profits. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
